Description: This inspirational video, from Youtube creator TheGaroStudios, combines scenes from a number of films and television programs (including Into the Wild, Dead Poets Society, Wild, and Vikings), to form a single motivational message. It is intended to remind the viewer how precious life is and encourages the audience to live fully and deliberately.

The Flemish Radio Choir performs Samuel Barber’s Agnes Dei, Opus 11, in Brussels. Agnus Dei (“Lamb of God”) comes from John 1:29 and is a part of the Latin liturgical tradition. The words of the song are a request for peace and forgiveness. In 1967, Barber set the Latin words of the liturgical Agnus Dei, a part of the Mass, for mixed chorus with optional organ or piano accompaniment.

Father Serafim Bitbunov and the choir of the Thirteen Holy Assyrian Fathers monastery perform a psalm in Aramaic that moves Pope Francis to tears during his visit to Svetitskhoveli Orthodox Cathedral in Mtskheta, Georgia. The Aramaic languages are an ancient branch of the Semitic language family, and there is scholarly consensus that the historical Jesus spoke Aramaic.

Claude Debussy’s “Clair de Lune,” (Suite bergamasque, CD 82, L. 75: III.), is one of the most well-known musical pieces of all time. It was inspired by the poem “Clair de lune” (“Moonlight”), by French poet Paul Verlaine. In Symbolist style, the poem’s imagery of masks, dancing, and moonlight evokes a particular mood that is well reflected in Debussy’s composition.

In this scene from the science fiction film Cloud Atlas, the narrator reflect on his trials and tribulations that seem to be universal, across both time and people. However, he spends his final moments, before his planned suicide, writing a note to his lover, focusing on the light that their love brought to his otherwise dark and insurmountable struggles.

Choir! Choir! Choir! began as a weekly drop-in singing event, equal parts singing, comedy, and community-building. In 2015, 1500 singers came to Luminato Festival in Toronto for a very special event. Choir! leaders taught them backup parts to Leonard Cohen's Hallelujah, and Rufus Wainwright joined the crowd on stage to lead the vocals. The collective performance amplifies the power of the musical piece.

The Laughing Heart is a classic poem by Charles Bukowski, that takes on the universal human condition of life and death. It acknowledges the darkness in life, but encourages us to find and cultivate the light. Written in 1993 and published posthumously by Black Sparrow Press in 1996, “The Laughing Heart” is a testament to the clarity that he found at the end of his life.

De Ushuaia a La Quiaca (From Ushuaia to La Quiaca) by Gustavo Santaolalla is the result of an epic road trip from the northernmost tip of his native Argentina to the southernmost town. Between 1981 and 1985, Santaolalla was producer and instrumentalist on a monumental tour (also called De Ushuaia a La Quiaca) where Argentine singer-songwriting León Gieco visited folk musicians across the entire country in their own homes, and recorded with them. This haunting track comes out of that experience.

Pema Chodron is an American Tibetan Buddhist nun and a leading meditation teacher, known for her down-to-earth interpretations for Western audiences. In this 2007 talk at the Omega Institute, she offers practical advice for what to do when “you're about to lose it.”

Description: Mary Oliver’s “Wild Geese” is a poetic guide to leading a peaceful and authentic life. Instead of striving for perfection, one may find perfection in connecting with themself, just as they are. Oliver’s work is inspired by nature and reminds us of humans’ place within nature, that we are part of a larger ecosystem with its own rhythms that are greater than human constructs and troubles.
